subject.title: Codex PreToolUse native hook relay spawns CPU-bound openclaw-hooks processes and stalls gateway RPC

question: Which supported protection should own the remaining active-policy Codex relay load: a lightweight/resident relay path, pre-exec bounded concurrency, tool-scoped matching, or a deliberately combined design?
rationale: The existing narrow opt-out preserves policy relays, but choosing how to reduce their remaining cost changes native tool-policy enforcement, runtime architecture, and operator behavior.

options.title: Sponsor a combined safety path
options.body: Use matcher/no-work omission to reduce avoidable launches and define a lightweight or pre-exec bounded path for the remaining policy-required relays, with policy-preservation load proof.

options.title: Land scope reduction first
options.body: Review the linked matcher work as an incremental reduction in spawn rate, while tracking bounded active-policy relay execution as follow-up work.

options.title: Adopt an operator-only mitigation
options.body: Document the narrow loop-detection opt-out as the supported short-term recovery path and defer runtime architecture changes.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a combined safety path
recommendation.body: Use matcher/no-work omission to reduce avoidable launches and define a lightweight or pre-exec bounded path for the remaining policy-required relays, with policy-preservation load proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their linked proposal covers the spawn-decision boundary and explicitly identifies the policy-preservation tradeoff that needs direction.
